source.publication: 2025 DR 0104 Booklet (Colorado Individual Income Tax), DR 0104 and DR 0104AD
source.section: DR 0104AD line 3 / line 5 Social Security Benefits (PDF p.18 Line 3; p.19 Line 5; DR 0104AD p.1 lines 3 and 5), 65 or older ('the entire amount'); DR 0104 lines 1, 10-13 (PDF p.8, p.10); tax table PDF p.34-35

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (you) 30,000.00 + taxable Social Security 11,300.00 = 41,300.00. Taxable Social Security on gross benefits 24,000.00 (you): federal SS worksheet (given): half of benefits 12,000.00 + other income 30,000.00 = 42,000.00; less 25,000.00 = 17,000.00; line 11 = 8,000.00; line 13 = half of smaller of 17,000.00 and 9,000.00 = 4,500.00; line 14 = 4,500.00; line 15 = 85% x 8,000.00 = 6,800.00; line 16 = 11,300.00; 85% of benefits = 20,400.00; taxable Social Security = 11,300.00. Federal taxable income = 41,300.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - 1 x 2,000.00 additional for age 65 or older = 23,550.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). DR 0104 line 1 federal taxable income (Form 1040 line 15) 23,550.00; lines 2-9 additions 0.00 (no state income tax addback, no other-state bond interest; federal AGI 41,300.00 is not over 300,000, so no line 4 deduction addback); line 10 subtotal 23,550.00. DR 0104AD: Line 3 (primary taxpayer, age 70, 65 or older): entire taxable Social Security 11,300.00. Line 22 subtotal = 11,300.00; DR 0104 line 11 = 11,300.00. Line 12 Colorado taxable income = 23,550.00 - 11,300.00 = 12,250.00. Line 13 tax = 4.4% x 12,250.00 = 539.00 (the tax table row over 12,200.00 but not over 12,300.00, PDF p.34, gives 539.00; expected keeps the formula figure). No credits claimed: 0.00. Colorado income tax 539.00.
accepted_approximations: Tax is figured on the exact income at 4.4%; below 50,000 the booklet uses the tax table, which taxes each 100-dollar row at its midpoint and rounds to the dollar.
